content.comment_body: Hello, I'm encountering an issue with my latest [product_name] installation. I have a [article_no] unit with three modules: one [product_name] and two [product_name] modules. Four PT100 sensors are connected using three wires. While AI2, AI3, and AI4 provide correct readings, AI1 consistently shows about 10 degrees higher than the actual temperature. Even after deleting the program and installing a minimal one, the incorrect value persists on AI1, leading me to believe the issue isn't software-related. I've also tried swapping module positions and using different PT100 sensors, but AI1 remains affected. Thanks in advance for any assistance!
After the analog input, make sure to connect the analog amplifier block. In the parameters menu, set the sensor type to PT100 according to your application.
Thank you, the problem is resolved! One amplifier had its configuration set to 'no sensor', which was causing the error.

analysis.insight_summary: A user encountered an incorrect temperature reading on the AI1 channel when using RTD modules with PT100 sensors. Standard troubleshooting, including module swapping and program resets, did not resolve the issue. It was found that the amplifier block for AI1 was misconfigured as 'no sensor' rather than PT100, highlighting a lack of clear feedback in the system to help users quickly identify configuration errors.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect all analog inputs to provide reliable and accurate sensor readings, straightforward configuration guidance, and instant feedback that helps them pinpoint mismatches between sensor setup and input configuration.
